name: Measure a thickness with a 0-1 in outside micrometer, the part resting on the bench

working.role: turns the thimble and the ratchet stop

steadying.role: holds the frame and sets the anvil square on the part; a ratchet-stop micrometer is not for one-handed use

phases.what: Both hands to the micrometer on the bench
The steadying hand takes the frame; the working hand's thumb and fingertips go to the thimble [proposed: duration_s]
Clean the faces: close the spindle lightly on a slip of lint-free paper, then draw the paper out slowly
phases.ends_on: the paper out, the faces wiped

phases.what: Zero: bring the spindle onto the anvil, turn the ratchet stop 1.5 to 2 turns, read zero [proposed: duration_s]
phases.ends_on: 0.000 on the scale, the ratchet clicking over

phases.what: Spin the thimble open a little wider than the thickness [proposed: duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the gap a little wider than the part

phases.what: The steadying hand sets the anvil flat on the part's face, the frame square to it [proposed: duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the anvil flat on the face

phases.what: Turn the thimble to bring the spindle down slowly onto the other face [proposed: duration_s]
Turn the ratchet stop 1.5 to 2 turns: it clicks over and holds the constant measuring force [proposed: duration_s]
Read the sleeve and thimble with the eye square to the index line: read from above or below, the lines are misread [proposed: duration_s]
Back the spindle off and lift the micrometer clear of the part [proposed: turns, duration_s]
Set it down on the bench [proposed: duration_s]

sources.ref: Mitutoyo Europe, 'Handheld Measuring Instruments: a guide to proper use, maintenance and care' (PRE1436), Outside Micrometers and All Instruments
sources.gives: always use the ratchet stop; bring the faces into contact slowly, then turn the ratchet stop 1.5 to 2 turns; ratchet micrometers hold a measuring force of 5-10 N; clean the faces by closing them on lint-free paper and drawing it out; a hand warms the frame, so measure quickly

sources.ref: Mitutoyo, Quick Guide to Precision Measuring Instruments, Catalog No. E11003(7): Micrometers
sources.gives: a ratchet stop is unsuitable for one-handed operation; wipe the faces and set zero before measuring; read square to the index line, as an angle causes parallax error

sources.ref: Kurt, 'Double Station Manual Vise Setup' (YouTube), measured locally with MediaPipe Hand Landmarker; borrowed, as this tool's own footage is edited and tracks too few moves to time a reach
sources.gives: reach durations: the right hand's interquartile range, 0.32-0.67 s

sources.ref: Mitutoyo America, 'Check Points for Measuring Instruments: Digimatic Outside Micrometer', measured locally with MediaPipe Hand Landmarker
sources.gives: both hands on the micrometer, the right at the thimble and the left holding the frame; the faces cleaned on paper in about 6 s

notes: Both hands are on the micrometer because Mitutoyo rules out one-handed use of a ratchet stop, and Mitutoyo's own footage holds it that way, the right hand at the thimble and the left on the frame; the part lies on the bench, so neither hand holds it. In that footage the fingers turn the thimble while the hand barely rolls (median 6-9 deg/s), so the wrist should stay nearly still in #4, #5, #7 and #8. The 5-10 N is Mitutoyo's figure for ratchet micrometers, which a dealer listing also gives for the 103-177. mic1 reads 0-1 in, so nist-ftc-10's 31 mm height in its inspection step is beyond it: that needs a 1-2 in micrometer or the height gauge. Hold the frame no longer than needed, since body heat expands it (Mitutoyo). The grasps are this card's reading of Mitutoyo's words. Proposed, with reasons (phase numbers count from 1): every duration but the reach and the cleaning (#3, timed from Mitutoyo's footage), since no source times them: #2 0.6 s, #4 2.0 s, #5 2-4 s, #6 1.0 s, #7 1.5-3 s, #8 1.5 s, #9 2.0 s, #10 1.0 s, #11 0.6 s; #10 backing off one turn and lifting clear, and #11 setting it down, which no source describes, so neither has one.
